newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative Clarke denies offering Hague job.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative Clarke denies offering Hague job.

text.p: Britain's former Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, one of the front-runners in the Conservative Party leadership campaign, denied on Wednesday he would offer rival candidate William Hague a role, possibly as his deputy leader.
But he told BBC radio he would make "an important announcement" later on Wednesday.

The Independent newspaper reported that Conservatives were talking of Clarke, the only Europhile of six leadership contenders, running on a "dream ticket" with Hague, the former Welsh Secretary, who is only 36.

"This afternoon I am holding my first press conference of the leadership campaign and I do intend to make an important announcement," Clarke said. "Sadly for The Independent it is not the one reported in their paper."
But he said his announcement would be relevant to that story. "I think I have more members of parliament likely to vote for me than any other candidate," he said.
Hague's campaign received a boost on Tuesday when he won the backing of former minister Lord Parkinson. The bookmakers make Hague a 5/4 favourite to take the reins of the opposition party.
